decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY captures the endpoint-height options but leaves stale reach-study status and geometry descriptions and omits the Hero V's proportional scaling rule.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Abdulbari,

Somewhere my intended message got lost in translation. I know it’s hard to read my mind when I use more abstract terms, and I think I was trying to ask you to change too many things at once, which is why we have taken a couple of steps in the wrong direction.

I’m attaching this image for reference because it was the closest rendering to what I wanted to refine. Instead of changing the length and exploring the terminations at the same time, we’re going to focus strictly on height.

Could you please show the following as a calibrated progression in both the Hero V and the second V? The second V should remain proportionally scaled to its own size, so each increase should be calculated relative to the total height of that individual V.

Original Option B as the control
Original Option B with the right endpoint approximately 1% higher
The same treatment at approximately 2% higher
The same treatment at approximately 3% higher

Please keep the existing slope, terminal shape, taper, and all other geometry exactly as shown in the original Option B. Only the height of the right endpoint should change. Once the correct percentage is established, the É accent should follow that same proportional relationship.

I know this is an exceptionally small distinction, but I believe the relationship between the left and right endpoints will become one of the defining details shared across the Hero V, second V, and É accent. I want it to be almost imperceptible, but still enough to distinguish it from a more average V.

Thank you for helping me isolate it with this level of precision.

value_updates.endpoint_height_scaling_rule: Calculate each increase relative to the Hero V's own total height

The client ends the active length-and-terminal comparison, restores original Option B as the control, and locks the terminal shape and taper while endpoint height alone is studied.

decisions.reason: The calibrated study concerns only the Hero V, second V, and subsequent É accent relationship; it does not change the E or L letterform requirements.
The source changes the second V's endpoint-height study but does not alter its established subordinate hierarchy relative to the Hero V, É accent, E, or L.
The source directs the É accent to follow the selected proportional endpoint relationship but does not revoke or modify the existing exact peak-alignment requirement.
The endpoint-height study leaves the Satin Reflection finish and champagne-gold distribution unchanged.
The client explicitly isolates endpoint height while keeping other geometry unchanged and makes no change to the selected Balanced Flow kerning.
Changing the V endpoints does not change the established E/L cap-height rule based on the second V's left arm.
The source refines glyph geometry and does not change the obligation to explain design rationale with review rounds.
The right-endpoint height study does not change the common baseline defined by the bottom points of the two Vs and the E/L baseline.
The source contains no decision about attachment or proof-file formats.
